Astrophysicist Neil deGrasse Tyson sits down with Joe Rogan in a segment from the Joe Rogan Experience, the long-form interview podcast Rogan has hosted for years. Tyson, one of the best-known science voices in America, takes up a subject the show returns to often: UFO reports and what they really prove.

Tyson lays out a skeptic's case, asking what kind of proof a claim as big as alien visitors would need. He pushes on weak photos, second-hand stories, and the gap between seeing something odd and knowing what it was. Rogan presses back, and the clash between belief and hard proof drives the talk.

Joe Rogan asks if UFO films are in fact films of hypersonic missiles in a segment from his show. The guest take here is a skeptic's one: the odd craft on tape may be our own best arms at test. Rogan hosts the check.

Rogan works through the top films and what a fast missile could and could not do on tape. He weighs the claims of pilots who say the craft moved past all known arms. The segment is short and sharp. Listeners get a cold splash on hot lore. The library holds the file as an archive record of the debate.
